correctness.rationale: All hypotheses and quantifiers are explicit. In transformed coordinates, U=(I-2Q)(I-2P) is orthogonal with symmetric part I-2(P-Q)^2; C=D^(1/2)UD^(1/2) has C+C^T>=2cos(2θ)D and C^TC<=LD. Expanding (I-ηC)^T(I-ηC) yields the claimed squared norm contraction, uniform across all approximate projectors and iterations. For H=Ldiag(-1,1) the two-reflection product is planar rotation ±2θ, yielding exact squared amplification 1-2ηLcos(2θ)+(ηL)^2. This proves both sharp frontiers and endpoint non-strictness. Standalone standard-library exact rational verifier passes 2D, 4D, 6D contraction certificates plus sharpness tests; independent numerical stress of 1,000 instances is non-proving corroboration.

originality.rationale: Primary full-text comparison: arXiv:2603.25390v2 §5 / Theorem 5.2 gives a sufficient small projector error at a fixed step in the M-norm, rather than an iff universal principal-angle and step-size phase diagram in the absolute-Hessian energy norm, allowing arbitrary frame switching. value.rationale: Inexact unstable-subspace estimation is a central computational concern of p-HiSD. The motivating 2026 theorem gives a condition-number-dependent small projector error for a prescribed fixed step; this result instead provides an explicit and sharp joint angular tolerance/stepsize tradeoff for exact quadratic models, including arbitrarily varying eigensolver errors. The two-dimensional necessary witness makes the step law actionable as a worst-case safeguard and separates absolute-Hessian energy convergence from ordinary metric-norm claims. This is a structural robustness boundary, not an arbitrary parameter tabulation or asserted general nonlinear theorem.
